system_description.narrative_title: Escalation by Economic Targeting in the Russia–Ukraine War
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is an intensifying Russia–Ukraine conflict in which drone and missile strikes increasingly target economic and civilian infrastructure (warehouses, retail, refineries), prompting Russian mobilization signals and expanded European military and financial support for Ukraine. As an open system it admits flows of weapons, intelligence, political pressure, money and information across borders; those inputs and outputs create reinforcing feedbacks (escalation → counter‑escalation → mobilization → foreign aid) and cross‑sector spillovers into markets, domestic politics and supply chains. Key systemic variables are military capability (drones, missiles, air defences), economic vulnerability of infrastructure and logistics, political legitimacy/mobilization, and international support/sanctions dynamics.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: kinetic operations between Russia and Ukraine (including cross‑border strikes and drone campaigns); targeting of economic infrastructure (retail logistics, refineries, chemical plants); Russian domestic responses (mobilisation, legal powers over infrastructure); Ukrainian political decisions and battlefield strategy; European and NATO military deliveries, funding and diplomatic coordination; sanctions, intelligence cooperation and information warfare affecting markets and public opinion.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical and security order (great‑power competition, international institutions, global markets and supply chains).
adjacent_subsystems: European domestic politics and elections (political stability, wartime political debates)
Global energy and commodity markets (oil, gas, critical minerals, supply chains)
International finance and sanctions/private capital flows (investor risk, asset deals, aid funding)
Defense technology and arms markets (drones, air‑defence, AI-enabled systems)

variables.name: Military capability
variables.description: The aggregate level of available offensive and defensive military resources, platforms and operational readiness.

variables.name: Economic target strike rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of kinetic strikes explicitly aimed at economic and civilian infrastructure per unit time.

variables.name: Economic infrastructure vulnerability
variables.description: The susceptibility of logistics, energy, industrial and commercial facilities to damage, outage and cascading failure.

variables.name: Logistics network resilience
variables.description: The capacity of transport, storage and distribution networks to maintain function and recover from disruptions.

variables.name: Air defense effectiveness
variables.description: The probability and rate at which air defenses detect, track and successfully intercept incoming aerial threats.

variables.name: Political mobilization
variables.description: The degree of domestic political support, mobilization willingness and legitimacy for wartime policies and measures.

variables.name: International support flow
variables.description: The rate and volume of external transfers of military equipment, funding, intelligence and advisory assistance.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure
variables.description: The intensity and economic impact of externally imposed trade, financial and transaction restrictions.

variables.name: Defense industry output
variables.description: The production and delivery rate of weapons, munitions, air‑defense systems and related military materiel.

variables.name: Information warfare intensity
variables.description: The scale, reach and effectiveness of coordinated messaging, influence operations, cyber operations and propaganda.

variables.name: Market disruption
variables.description: The level of volatility and functional disruption in financial, insurance and commodity markets linked to the conflict.

variables.name: Civilian casualty rate
variables.description: The rate at which noncombatant deaths and injuries occur as a result of military operations and strikes.

variables.name: Legal control over infrastructure
variables.description: The extent and scope of legal authorities to seize, operate, restrict or compel use of critical infrastructure assets.

variables.name: Cross-border weapon flow
variables.description: The rate of movement of arms, munitions and dual‑use materiel across borders and through illicit channels.

variables.name: Critical supply risk
variables.description: The exposure of key material, component and energy supply chains to interruption, scarcity or rerouting.

variables.name: Public support for external aid
variables.description: The level of public opinion in external societies favoring provision of military, financial or humanitarian assistance.

catalysts.title: Ukraine intensifies strikes on Russian retail/logistics
catalysts.description: Continued Ukrainian drone and missile strikes on Russian online retailers and logistics hubs (eg Ozon) are likely to persist, increasing economic targeting pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukrainian drones kill at least 10, hit warehouse of Russian online retailer Ozon'; 'Ukraine targets Ozon in widening attacks'.

catalysts.title: Russian state seizure of vulnerable infrastructure
catalysts.description: Implementation of new Kremlin authority to take control of infrastructure deemed vulnerable to drone attacks, including seizures and military protection measures.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Putin hands Russian state right to take control of badly protected infrastructure objects'; 'Putin allows Russia to take control of infrastructure...'.

catalysts.title: Accelerated allied air‑defence and missile deliveries
catalysts.description: France, UK and other European allies accelerate deliveries of air-defence systems and missiles, backed by EU funding packages.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'France agrees to accelerate air defence deliveries'; 'France, UK step up missile support'; 'EU approves further €6.1 billion for Ukraine's defence.'

catalysts.title: Potential Russian mobilization after September election
catalysts.description: Statements that Putin will draft additional troops after September elections imply renewed mobilization and force generation in the coming months.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Putin will draft 300,000 new troops after September elections, Zelenskiy says'; 'Russia Tests Readiness for New Round of Military Mobilization.'

catalysts.title: Norway pledged $9bn+ to Ukraine in 2027
catalysts.description: Norway's announced multi‑billion funding package for 2027 is a scheduled external support flow that will bolster Ukraine's resources next year.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Norway to give over $9 billion to Ukraine in 2027.'

catalysts.title: UK plan to support long‑range missile production
catalysts.description: UK ministerial visits and pledges to back long‑range missile production for Ukraine, including technical and industrial assistance.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'UK's Burnham to visit Ukraine with plan to support long-range missile production.'

catalysts.title: U.S. mediation window (through summer 2027)
catalysts.description: Zelenskiy's indication of a U.S. mediation window that could drive diplomatic activity and potential de‑escalation if exploited.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Ukraine's Zelenskiy sees window for U.S. mediation until summer 2027.'

catalysts.title: Escalating drone strikes on energy/refinery sites
catalysts.description: Repeated drone attacks on oil refineries and chemical complexes signal a likely continuation of strikes against energy infrastructure, disrupting production.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russia's Perm oil refinery halted operations after August 21 drone attack'; 'Russia's Afipsky oil refinery on fire after drone attack.'
